definition: A gradation is one step in a gradual, ordered series — a slight, orderly shift in shade, degree, or stage between one level and the next.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word gradation. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know gradation should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The paint store's sample wall held forty gradations of white, and Nadia could no longer tell where 'ivory' surrendered to 'bone.'
A nuance is fainter than a gradation — a difference so slight that most eyes miss it entirely, while a gradation is a step you can point to on the scale.
A contrast is stronger than a gradation: a gradation eases from one level to the next by a visible step, while a contrast sets two levels boldly against each other, plain at a glance.

Shading is the painter's word for continuous, blended change — one tone melting into the next with no steps at all. A gradation keeps its steps: you can point to where one level ends and the next begins.

An increment is a measured, usually equal addition — the thermostat's two degrees, the annual raise. A gradation may be too subtle to measure at all; what it promises is not a fixed amount but a scale that moves by degrees.

A gradation is one step in a gradual, ordered series — a slight, orderly shift in shade, degree, or stage between one level and the next.

The luthier's sandpaper rack ran from 80-grit to 2000, and the apprentice's first month went to learning its gradations — which step erases the scratches the last one left, and why skipping two steps costs an afternoon.
Gradation is the word for each of those orderly steps on a scale, and for the step-by-step climb they make together.
The change comes by degrees, every level defined by its neighbors above and below.
Where difference blends smoothly with no steps at all, shading is the better word; where it jumps all at once, a leap; the gradation lives between them — difference taken one step at a time.
Gradation is for scales: color charts, registers of politeness, degrees of severity.

Two neighbors to keep straight — a spectrum is the whole range laid end to end, while a gradation is one step within it; and a grade is the rank assigned, while a gradation is the interval a scale climbs by.
If the change happens all at once, the word you want is leap or break, not gradation.

In the darkroom, Marisol never guesses at exposure.
She cuts a test strip and exposes it in bands: two seconds, four, six, eight, ten, each band a shade darker than the last.
Developed, the strip shows a clean gradation of gray running from near-white to near-black, and she can set a fingernail on the exact line where one band ends and the next begins.
Her teacher calls the strip a ladder of tones and warns that a print is ruined when the rungs blur together; the eye must be able to climb them one at a time.
Marisol picks the band she wants, reads its time, and exposes the full sheet with no guesswork left.
